5	### Overview
6	The milk-testing scandal spanning 1889–1925 involves allegations of cream theft or water addition at Ostrey Hollow skimming station in Ordell County. The case was exonerated in 1958, 35 years after dismissal and 24 years after the death of accused tester Ansel Keddie. Scientific analysis proved defective glassware—milk pipettes that delivered only 95% of marked capacity—caused consistently low test results recorded from 1897 to June 1923.
